# Researching and ingesting wiki evidence

Choose the mode explicitly from the request. An unspecified request to use this
role is not permission to process the whole backlog; clarify the intended task.
Treat `` as the request when the host has not substituted it.

- **Discover sources on a topic:** read [discovery](references/discover.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md),
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md), and
  [efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md). Research perspectives
  return candidates without writing. When delegation is available, use separate
  read-only finders and keep the selector independent of the sources it found.
  Complete that selection before opening a capture operation; a self-selected
  list does not fulfill independent research. Use the capture route only within the
  requested scope; a request for candidates alone remains read-only.
- **Capture named URLs or saved web pages:** read [named capture](references/capture.md)
  and [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md). Skip broad topic research;
  preserve deduplication, declines and capture checks.
- **Capture a named format or service:** read its complete route:
  [PDF](references/clip-pdf.md), [Word](references/clip-docx.md),
  [PowerPoint](references/clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheets](references/clip-xlsx.md),
  [GitHub repository](references/clip-gh.md), or
  [Confluence](references/clip-confluence.md). These routes include prerequisite
  checks; missing converters or authentication never justify fabricated evidence.
- **Ingest named existing clippings:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), and
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md). Use the exact source set;
  do not rediscover it or silently expand to the global backlog.
- **Process new or un-ingested clippings without a filename:** read
  [ingestion](references/ingest.md) and the
  [hash-join backlog contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md).
  Determine eligibility before writing. Preserve already summarized sources and
  reject restricted evidence as support. If nothing eligible is pending, report
  that without opening an operation, logging, committing or refreshing indexes.

research-and-ingest flow already provides it. Only capture tools write raw
artifacts, and agents never edit their bodies. Read
[evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before assessing fidelity,
quoting or synthesizing; preserve restrictions and platform-specific sections.

[operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md). Finish the
scoped validation, log, commit, sync and remote verification unless publication
is held. Reuse an enclosing operation when it owns the work; preserve other
writers' edits. For concept reuse and relationship changes read
[efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md).

# Discover sources on a topic

Given a topic, find and independently assess sources that fill an evidence gap.
Perspective passes return candidates and never write the vault. A candidates-only
request stays read-only: report the selection without declines or captures. When
capture is within scope, use [capture and completion](capture.md#capture-the-selected-sources).
Ingestion is a separate authorized mode.

## Independence checkpoint before capture

Topic discovery requires the five perspective passes below and independent
selection. When the host provides delegation, actually dispatch read-only
finders; do not replace their execution with a list you found and scored yourself.
The orchestrator may select their returned candidates, or a separate reviewer
may select them. A finder must not grade its own finds. A small or controlled
source corpus does not remove this separation.

Before opening an operation or calling a clipper, retain the returned candidate
lists and the independent selection with its credibility reasons. If delegation
is unavailable, use the documented sequential lenses and disclose that limit;
do not claim an independent pass that did not run. Named-source capture skips
topic discovery and uses [capture](capture.md) directly.

## Phase 0 — dedup before searching
Gather what the wiki already has so the search hunts for *gaps*, not dupes:
- Known source URLs: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/known-urls.mjs"` prints
  them, one per line, normalized as the clipper normalizes them (`--count` prints
  the number). It reads the clippings themselves (the first `source:` line of each
  file directly under `raw/clippings`), rather than querying an index built from
  them — the shortest path to the fact, and it stays correct while the index is
  stale. To ask about particular candidates, use
  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/known-urls.mjs" --check "<url>" "<url>"`: one line
  per URL, in the order given, `new`, `clipped raw/clippings/<name>.md` (with
  ` (+N recapture)` when later captures of the page exist) or `declined: <reason>`.
  `--summary --topic "<topic>"` prints what a topic already holds. All three only read.
- Coverage summary: name the unanswered question, run bounded wiki searches, and
  read the relevant task MOC and leading concept/synthesis pages. Read only the
  manual Start here section of `index.md` if orientation is needed; do not load
  the generated catalog. List the known coverage and the specific evidence gap.
- Sanity-check the set: if the vault has clippings on disk but the known-URL
  set is empty, STOP — the collection step failed; do not proceed to search.
Pass the known-URL set + a one-line "already covered" summary to every perspective.

## Phase 1 — five perspective researchers (parallel if supported, else sequential)
Each perspective gets: the topic, the known-URL set, the coverage summary, and its
lens. Run them **in parallel if your host supports agent fan-out** — Claude Code:
dispatch five read-only agents in one message via the Agent tool; Copilot CLI: use
custom agents — **otherwise run the five lenses sequentially yourself.** Each runs
2–3 *varied* web searches, pre-skips any result whose domain is on the blocklist,
fetches the promising hits, and **returns a ranked candidate list** — it writes
nothing. Lenses:
- **Academic** — papers, textbooks, primary research, .edu.
- **Technical** — official docs, specs, standards, source repos.
- **Applied** — case studies, real-world usage, tutorials from practitioners.
- **News/Trends** — recent developments, reputable reporting (last ~2 years).
- **Contrarian** — critiques, failure modes, dissenting analysis.

Each candidate: `{ title, url, quality_guess: high|medium|low, key_findings,
why_ingest, adds_evidence, changes_page }`. `adds_evidence` names the unanswered
question it helps settle; `changes_page` names an existing or proposed concept
or synthesis. More material on an already answered question is not automatically
an improvement. Inspect existing high-use stubs and missing bridges before
requesting another broad collection run.

## Phase 2 — independent select + credibility (do NOT let a finder grade itself)
As the orchestrator (or a separate reviewer), over the pooled candidates:
1. Dedup by URL (normalize: drop `#fragment`, trailing `/`); drop any already in the
   known-URL set; drop blocked domains; drop any in the decline log
   (`.wiki-master/declined.json` — clip.mjs enforces this too, but skipping here
   saves re-arguing settled candidates).
2. Score each survivor with the rubric → `high | medium | low`:
   - +2 peer-reviewed / primary / official
   - +1 recent (≤3 yr) where recency matters
   - +1 known/credentialed author or authoritative org
   - +1 corroborated by another perspective's find (max +1)
   - −1 vendor-primary / promotional / single-blogger opinion
   Tiers: **high** ≥4, **medium** 2–3, **low** 0–1, **reject** <0 (don't clip).
3. Keep the top sources (favor `high`/`medium`; a few `low` are fine if on-topic).
   Reddit posts/comments and Medium articles are eligible; assess each source
   using the rubric, without treating votes as credibility. In the ranked report,
   group them under `## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` and `## Medium articles`
   respectively, and carry those sections into ingestion per the
   [Reddit and Medium evidence policy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md#reddit-and-medium).
4. **Only when capture is authorized, before the first decline or clip write**, open a discover operation with
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op discover` and retain its
   token using the host-specific completion example. Reuse that operation below, and
   pass its token as `--since <token>` on every clip: each clipper then records the exact
   path of every file it writes in the operation's ledger.
   **Record every reject** so it is never re-litigated:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --decline="<one-line reason>"`.
   "Seen, considered, declined" must have a representation — an unrecorded reject
   is indistinguishable from "never seen" and comes back every run. Declines
   expire after 180 days (TTL), so a changed world gets one re-evaluation.
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/decline.mjs" list` (`--json` for a machine reading)
   and `show "<url>"` read the log without changing it. `supersede "<url>" --reason "<why>"`
   ends an active decline without clipping anything; it is the only way to do so for a URL
   already in the vault, because `--supersede-decline` on a clip takes effect only when a
   clipping is written.


Continue with [capture and completion](capture.md#capture-the-selected-sources)
for approved-scope survivors, or return the candidate report for a research-only
request. Named URLs and saved files use [named capture](capture.md) directly.
# Vault access and host commands

Resolve the plugin root from the installed `SKILL.md` location, not the current
working directory: its containing skill folder's `../../` is the plugin root.
From a file in a skill's `references/` folder, use `../../../` instead.
Resolve and quote absolute helper paths before running commands. Treat
`$ARGUMENTS` as the user's request when the host has not substituted it. A linked
skill or reference can be read directly when the host has no skill loader; shared
policy does not require loading the maintenance-role entry point.
Resolve `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT` (default `~/.wiki-master-vault`; with `WIKI_MASTER_REQUIRE_VAULT=1` set and no vault named, a script stops with exit 2 instead of using the default) and verify the expected
vault layout. Read local `AGENTS.md` and schema before edits. A known root and
filesystem access are sufficient for the supported operations below; do not ask
the user to restart Obsidian as a prerequisite for all work.

## Layout and read scope

`raw/clippings/` holds captured evidence; `wiki/{sources,entities,concepts,syntheses,authored}/`
holds maintained pages; `moc/` holds navigational maps; `log/` holds one file per
operation. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it. Reads do not
open operations, write logs, commit or refresh indexes. Before any authorized
mutation, read [operation completion](operations.md); before quoting or
synthesizing, read [evidence](evidence.md).

Prefer bounded search and relevant MOCs to the generated catalog. Search
diagnostics describe coverage, not relevance: a stale index can omit useful pages.
Read current passages and disclose weak or failed channels. Index freshness is
distinct from factual review dates.

## Choose the supported channel

| Operation | Channel and fallback |
|---|---|
| Read a Markdown page or source | CLI `read path=...`, or read its exact path under the known vault root. |
| Search | Prefer `search.mjs` and inspect its diagnostics. If a channel fails, use available results plus bounded filesystem `rg` over `wiki/` and `moc/`; include `raw/clippings/` only for evidence lookup. State missing channels. |
| Health, evidence routes, identity, relationships, drift coverage | Bundled filesystem helpers work without Obsidian. Do not gate them on `assertRunning`. Drift embeddings still require their backend. |
| Factual freshness report | `stale.mjs` may use CLI discovery or scoped filesystem fallback. Preserve missing-review and coverage diagnostics. |
| Ordinary Markdown creation/editing | Use exact-path filesystem edits even when the CLI is healthy, with the same operation, evidence, schema and validation contract. Read current content before editing; preserve unrelated changes. Never pass a whole note body through `content=`. |
| Small typed property or app actions | Use the guarded CLI entry point below; filesystem property edits remain available with schema validation. |
| Opening a note in the UI, executing an Obsidian/plugin command, app state, live Bases queries | Requires working Obsidian CLI. Report the specific unavailable action; continue independent file work. Do not pretend a filesystem approximation executed an app action. |

For CLI calls use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" <command> ...`
or the bundled `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` API. These share an OS-managed lock across
agent processes, vaults and plugin copies for the same user. Do not launch native
`obsidian` directly or bypass a busy guard; other tools' raw calls are not protected.
The guard waits up to 10 seconds for a turn, then fails without sending a request.
Command execution has its own 10-second default timeout. Each request is limited
to a conservative 2,048-byte UTF-8 JSON envelope and rejects physical CR/LF/NUL.
This policy is not Obsidian's documented maximum. If rejected before sending,
use filesystem Markdown editing or narrow the read query; do not split a note
into many CLI writes or disable the guard. No fallback performs writes implicitly.
After an unavailable CLI or timeout, choose the supported fallback once; never
loop waiting for the app. **A timed-out mutation has an uncertain outcome.** Read
the exact target and check the intended effect before retrying or switching to
filesystem writes. An exit or timeout alone does not establish that nothing ran.
OS cleanup releases a lock after process death, but cannot prove a surviving CLI
child or an already-submitted Obsidian mutation finished. Inspect uncertain targets.

Validate resolved paths stay under the known root. Restrict searches to explicit
content directories; exclude `.recycle/`, dot folders, dependency trees and binary
originals. Do not recursively enumerate the entire user profile or scan a recycled
topic. Raw bodies remain immutable even during fallback. If target content changed
since it was read, reconcile it before writing; do not overwrite concurrent work.

## Shell portability

Examples elsewhere use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` as command
notation. Replace the placeholder with the actual installed absolute path before
execution, and set the vault for the operation's scope. Do not execute literal
angle-bracket placeholders or assume a relative `scripts/` path means the plugin.

PowerShell (restore any prior environment value):

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki health failed' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```

POSIX shell (one command's environment only):

```sh
WIKI_MASTER_VAULT='/absolute/path/to/vault' node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
```

On Windows, use PowerShell or the Node wrapper for Obsidian; Git Bash can select
the GUI executable instead of `Obsidian.com` and return misleading empty output.
These reporting examples are read-only: do not open an operation or rebuild the
index merely to answer a question.

WIKI_MASTER_VAULT=<SCRATCH>\candidate-flow
TMPDIR=<SCRATCH>/temporary/candidate-flow
WIKI_MASTER_REQUIRE_VAULT=1
TEMP=<SCRATCH>\temporary\candidate-flow
<CANDIDATE>/skills/wiki-researcher/references
Shell cwd was reset to <SCRATCH>\candidate-flow

# Capture named sources and research selections

A named URL or file request starts here, without broad web discovery or perspective
fan-out. Capture-only work never creates derived source or concept pages. For a
format-specific source, read its route before capture: [PDF](clip-pdf.md),

[GitHub repository](clip-gh.md), or [Confluence](clip-confluence.md).
Only read the matching route, then use its actual result and the shared completion
contract. The HTML mechanics below apply to ordinary web pages and supplied pages.

## Named sources
When the user names the pages to capture (URLs or saved files), there is nothing to
search for: skip broad research and discovery scoring. Dedup still applies to
the exact pages they named:
- Check them: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/known-urls.mjs" --check "<url>" "<url>"`
  (read-only; it needs no operation). The lines come back in the order given and carry no
  URL, so match them by position. `new`: clip it. `clipped raw/clippings/<name>.md`: it is
  already in the vault, so say so; if the user wants a second, dated copy of a page that has
  changed, clip it with `--recapture` (see the result table below).
  `declined: <reason>`: leave it, unless the user says the decline no longer holds; then
  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/decline.mjs" supersede "<url>" --reason "<why>"`, or
  `--supersede-decline="<why>"` on the clip.
- Clip the new ones using the capture procedure below, with `--topic="<topic>"` (the topic as the user gave it),
  `--quality=<tier>` and `--since <token>` on every clip.
- A page the user rejects is recorded, not forgotten:
  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --decline="<one-line reason>"`.
- Use the capture and completion contract below: open a discover operation
  before the first decline or clip, pass its token as `--since`, finish the capture
  with `op-ledger.mjs show` and `op-commit`. Ingest only when the exact source set
  is already authorized; a capture-only request ends after verified capture publication.
- A page the clipper cannot read (a login, a consent wall, an age check, a thin
  extraction) is saved by the user from a signed-in browser and supplied with
  `--from-file` (below).

## Capture the selected sources
Use the operation opened before the first decline or clip. If none is open, run
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op discover` before clipping
and retain its token; never overwrite a saved token. Do prerequisite and duplicate
checks first. When there is nothing to capture or decline, return without opening
an operation. Read-only named-URL dedup does not require broad coverage research.

For each kept candidate:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>`

**Pass `--topic` on every clip in the run, and use the same string for all of
them** — it is what lets maintainer triage group this run's leftovers together
later. Use the topic as the user gave it ($ARGUMENTS); do not re-word it per
source, or one run becomes several groups. The flag feeds both places a topic
can land: the clipping's frontmatter when the clip succeeds, and the triage log
when it fails, so you never have to know which happened.

**"Every clip" includes the non-HTML ones.** A candidate that is a PDF, a Word
file or a spreadsheet does not go through `clip.mjs` — it goes through
`clip-pdf.mjs`, `clip-docx.mjs` or `clip-xlsx.mjs` (see [PDF capture](clip-pdf.md) and
[Word capture](clip-docx.md)), and **every one of those takes `--topic` too**:

```bash
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs"  "<file.pdf>"  --source="<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-docx.mjs" "<file.docx>" --source="<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-xlsx.mjs" "<file.xlsx>" --source="<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
# clip-pptx.mjs takes the same options; clip-pdf also records the figure files it renders (--figures)
```

**A Confluence Cloud URL is HTML but also does not go through `clip.mjs`** — it
requires authentication `clip.mjs`'s anonymous fetch does not have, and reads
as thin content / gets auto-declined. Route it to [Confluence capture](clip-confluence.md) instead
(only applies if the `confluencer` plugin is installed — an optional runtime
dependency this one clipper alone takes on; see that reference for why):

```bash
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-confluence.mjs" "<confluence-url-or-page-id>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
```

Binary capture routes need the same topic string as HTML routes. Topic is
recorded going forward only; missing attribution leaves the resulting rows under
Unattributed. For a one-off named source outside a research run, omit the topic
rather than inventing one.

It blocks unreliable domains, skips dupes, extracts via Defuddle, and writes
`raw/clippings/<slug>.md` with `source`, `created`, `tags:[clippings]`, `quality`,
`topic`, `source-hash`. A `thin content` result means the page was a SPA/paywall — clip.mjs
records the decline automatically; report it for manual clipping (the user saves the page and you supply it with `--from-file <path>`, adding `--override-decline` because the decline was automatic), don't retry
blindly. A page that is a login form, a consent wall or an age check is not clipped even when it is long: its own vocabulary dominates the text and none of its title is in it (`lib/interstitial.mjs`). It is queued as `wrong-node` and is NOT declined, because a wall is not a verdict on the source; save it from a signed-in browser and supply it with `--from-file <path>`. A URL that looks like a text file (a checksum manifest, a pinned source file, anything on the raw GitHub host) is kept whole in a fence with `extraction: plaintext`, never judged thin; a binary or a file over 1 MiB served as text is refused and queued as `attention`. A `failed` result (403/transient) is NOT auto-declined — it may recover,
and a 180-day TTL would bury a source you still want.

**What a clip result means.** `clip.mjs` prints one result per URL:

| Result | Meaning | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| `clipped: raw/clippings/<name>.md` | written | cite that path |
| `duplicate (already clipped)` | this URL is already in the vault, also when another session wrote it first | nothing; do not clip it again. To keep a second, dated copy of a page that has changed, run the clip again with `--recapture` |
| `unchanged (same text as raw/clippings/<name>.md); nothing written` | `--recapture` found the page's text identical to a capture already held (exit 0) | nothing; the page has not changed |
| `recapture: not clipped yet, clipping it normally: <url>` | `--recapture` on a URL that was not in the vault; the line is followed by the ordinary result | read the result that follows |
| `clash: <url>: raw/clippings/<name>.md already exists ...` | the URL is new but every name it could have had was taken; **nothing was written** and one `attention` row is queued in triage | open the file named in the line and read its `source:` to see what holds the name, then re-run with `--slug=<name>`, or leave the row for maintainer triage |
| `declined`, `blocked`, `thin content`, `failed` | see below | see below |

A taken file name is a `clash`, never a `duplicate`: a `duplicate` always means the same URL.

**A second capture of a page already clipped.** `clip.mjs "<url>" --recapture --since <token>` fetches the page and runs the usual checks. If the text is new it writes a second clipping beside the first, named as the oldest capture's own name followed by ` (recaptured YYYY-MM-DD)`, with the same suffix on its `title`, `recapture-of` naming the newest existing capture, and `created` today; the older clipping is never edited. A second recapture on the same day with different text is a `clash`. `--slug=<name>` with `--recapture` is used exactly, with no suffix. Without the flag the same URL is a `duplicate`.

**A page a person saved.** `clip.mjs "<url>" --from-file <path> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>` records a page saved from a signed-in browser, with its real URL as `source` and nothing fetched. The file is `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt` (the page text) or `.html` or `.htm` (read by the same extractor as a fetched page), at most 1 MiB. The clipping carries `extraction: manual` and `supplied-sha256`, the SHA-256 of the file's bytes; the file's name is not recorded. The thin, login-form and decline checks apply as to any clip: a page under 100 words is queued as `thin` and is never declined, and a login, consent or age-gate page is queued as `wrong-node` and not written. A missing file, a folder, an empty path or an extension that is not one of those exits 2; a binary file or one over 1 MiB is queued as `attention`. `--from-file` on a URL already clipped is a `duplicate`, and with `--recapture` it writes a dated recapture. The clipper's refusal lines for a thin, wrong-node or login, consent or age-gate page say to use this route. `apply-reclips` refuses a clipping with `extraction: manual` (listed as refused, not a failure); to refresh one, save the page again and run `--from-file <path> --recapture`. The login-form check compares the page's title with its text, and it cannot judge a title with no word of five letters or more, for example a URL that ends in a bare id; a gate page supplied at such a URL is not caught.

**Names.** A page's title names its file. A document with no title and no heading is named from its URL path, nearest folder first, so `.../skills/one/SKILL.md` is `one-SKILL.md` and `.../skills/two/SKILL.md` is `two-SKILL.md`; the bare last segment is used only after the folders. The frontmatter `title:` stays exactly what the extractor returned, so `title: ""` on such a clipping is not a defect. A new clipping never ends `.md.md`; an older one may, and its name is still valid. A title another clipping already holds gets the distinguishing URL part added, for example `Smith v. Jones (93-1260.ZO)`. `--slug=<name>` chooses the file name without `.md`; a taken name is a clash and is never suffixed. `clip-pdf`, `clip-docx`, `clip-pptx` and `clip-xlsx` also take `--title="<text>"`, for a file whose name is not its title (`valve.pdf`), and `--slug=<name>`.

An option a clipper does not know exits 2 with its usage and clips nothing; `--help` prints the usage and clips nothing.

**Every unresolved link is queued for triage automatically.** `clip.mjs` records
`failed`, `thin`, and `wrong-node` outcomes to `.wiki-master/triage.jsonl`, so a
link that needs a human survives the terminal scrollback. Do not rely on your
completion report to carry them — point the user at [maintainer triage](../../wiki-maintainer/references/triage.md), where they can
disposition each one (retry, decline, clipped-by-hand). Queue anything else that
needs their judgement yourself with `recordIssue(vaultPath, { url, kind:
'attention', reason })`.

## Finish capture and report
Show the ranked list (title, url, quality, why), which clips succeeded, and which
were skipped (blocked, duplicate, thin, failed). If issues were queued, mention
maintainer triage and report their counts.

**Finish the capture operation before any decision pause.** The clipping set is what
the clippers recorded, not something to rebuild afterwards: run
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" show --since <saved-token> --out <ledger>`
and read its `raw/clippings/...` entries, exactly as written (a name with an em dash
included). The number of `raw/clippings/` entries must equal the number of clippings the
`clipped:` results reported (one per URL or file; `clip-gh` reports a file count, and
`clip-pdf --figures` adds `raw/figures/` entries that are not clippings); if it does not,
stop and find the difference. Never rebuild the set from `git show`, whose default output
quotes and escapes a non-ASCII name. Write one discovery log entry naming the
clipped/declined/failed counts (`log-entry.mjs ... --since <saved-token>`), run `show`
again, and close with:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op discover --title "<topic> → N clipped" --since <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger>`.
The `<ledger>` file you wrote outlives the close, so the ingest that follows takes its
clipping set from it.
Without `--paths-file` the close is refused while another operation is open. Verify the commit and push and verify remote publication through the shared
contract (`wiki-sync.mjs --op <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "<topic>"` closes and pushes in one command). If no writes occurred, report that and do not manufacture a log/commit.
Clippings must not remain dirty while waiting for an ingestion decision.

Then use the existing authorization for this exact source set:
- **Discover-and-ingest already authorized:** read [ingestion](ingest.md) and process the named
  successful clippings immediately. It owns a fresh operation and its own log.
  No second confirmation is needed.
- **Only discovery or capture authorized:** report the captured set and stop; do
  not create derived pages. If ingestion is subsequently requested, use the named
  set in a fresh operation.
- **Ingestion declined:** retain the committed clippings for manual review.

## Guardrails
- The perspective passes never write the vault; the matching clipping helper is the sole writer to its raw artifacts.
- Never edit the **body** of anything under `raw/` — clipped content is immutable
  source-of-truth. Frontmatter is pipeline state and may be updated by wiki-master
  tooling only (never by hand, never the body).
- Prefer primary/authoritative sources over open-publishing platforms.
- Ingestion requires authorization for this scope; existing explicit authorization
  satisfies this ingestion boundary. Do not add another confirmation to an approved discover-and-ingest run.
# Ingest captured evidence

Read [access and host commands](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md) before touching the vault. Also read for this operation: [evidence](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md).
Load the rest only when this run reaches it — [efficacy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md) before creating or merging a concept, alias or relationship; [maintenance](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md) when you compute the backlog with the content-hash join, or hit a structural repair.
Before the first authorized write, follow the shared operations completion contract; reuse existing session authorization.

## Select eligible work before opening an operation

For an explicit request to process new/un-ingested clippings without a filename,
run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs" --backlog`. The **not ingested
(no summary records their hash)** list is the starting set. This source-hash join,
including its documented legacy fallback, is authoritative for membership; do
not infer backlog from filenames, navigation citations or a successful exit.
An unspecified request to use the researcher role is not a request to ingest all.

For named clippings, resolve and read those exact paths only. Check the same
hash-join report and the existing source summaries before doing work: if a source
page already records that clipping's `source-hash`, preserve it and report already
ingested. A rerun creates no duplicate summary or unearned second ingestion.
An explicit request to revise an existing summary can update that canonical page;
do not expand named ingestion to unrelated backlog or broad discovery.

Inspect each selected clipping's metadata before treating it as support. Exclude
`citation-status: quarantined`, `restricted` or `retired` evidence, preserving its
raw bytes and restriction; report it separately rather than summarizing it as
accepted support. A missing source hash is a repair issue, not permission to
invent one. Binary originals and figure sidecars are not summary targets. The
helper's backlog can include restricted or defective captures, so its count is
not automatically the count of eligible work.

If the backlog is zero, every named source is already summarized, or no eligible
source remains, stop and report the actual result and any exclusions. Do not
create pages, open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes. For work that
remains, retain the exact eligible set and initial hash-join membership. See
[backlog semantics](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md) for migration
and repair cases; structural repair still needs its own authorized scope.

## Ingest and complete the selected set

Read [operation completion](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md)
before the first authorized write.

**Open the operation first:** `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op ingest`
This records what was already uncommitted, so the commit at the end contains your
work and not the user's in-progress writing. Close it in step 6.

**Keep the ledger as you go.** Record each page you write (`wiki/sources/...`, a concept
or synthesis you create or change) with
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" add --since <token> <path>...`, and give
`--since <token>` to `index-gen.mjs` and `log-entry.mjs`. When this ingest follows a discover
run, take the clipping set from that run's ledger file (its `raw/clippings/...` entries), not
from `git show`. Delegated writers get the parent token in their brief and run the same `add`
for the pages they write; they never close the operation (see the operations reference).

Prefer a named clipping set; two concurrent ingests can overwrite shared concept
pages, so coordinate overlapping targets rather than processing the global backlog
in parallel. Update only pages substantively changed by the evidence.

Apply the [Reddit and Medium evidence policy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md#reddit-and-medium)
to every page you write: Reddit-derived content belongs under
`## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` and Medium-derived content under
`## Medium articles`, including when updating a mixed-source page.

For each eligible source, perform steps 1–3 and preserve raw body bytes. After
the selected batch, perform steps 4–6 once so the operation has one log and commit:
1. Read the exact clipping through the guarded CLI or filesystem. Write derived
   Markdown through exact-path filesystem edits, never a whole CLI `content=` payload. Discuss
   the key takeaways with the user.
2. Write/update `wiki/sources/<slug>.md`: a summary with `sources: ["[[<raw link>]]"]`,
   `type: source`, `ai-generated: true`, and typed `created`/`updated`/`reviewed`.
   **Always quote each wikilink inside the list — `sources: ["[[A]]", "[[B]]"]`,
   never a bare `sources: [[A]]` or an unquoted block list (`- [[A]]`).** Both
   unquoted shapes look correct and Obsidian still renders the links, but neither
   is valid YAML: `[[A]]` is flow-sequence syntax one level too many and silently
   parses into a nested list instead of a string, which is exactly the "type
   mismatch, expected list" defect `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-inline-sources.mjs"`
   exists to repair in bulk. Quoting is what makes it an unambiguous string.
   **Cite the clipping by its actual filesystem path — `sources: ["[[raw/clippings/<exact filename>.md]]"]` — copied from the path you just read, never retyped from
   the source's title.** The clipper slugifies a title into a filename (`/`, `:`,
   `#`, `*`, `?`, quotes and brackets all become `-`, then a 120-char cap), so any
   title carrying one of those characters or running long does NOT name its own
   file. Citing the remembered title produces a link to a file that does not exist:
   the page becomes a `provenanceGap` and its clipping reads as unparsed, even
   though the ingest itself was correct. List the resolved vault's exact `raw/clippings/` directory or reuse the path
   from step 1 rather than reconstructing it.
   Also record `source-hashes: [<sha256>, …]` — the `source-hash` frontmatter value
   of each clipping you summarized (read it from the clipping's frontmatter). This
   is the machine key the ingest-backlog metric joins on — immune to filename and
   citation drift; the `sources: ["[[…]]"]` wikilink stays for navigation.
   To repair vaults that already drifted this way:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-provenance-links.mjs"` (dry run) then `--apply`.
   **Figures.** If the clipping's frontmatter lists `figures:`, open each sidecar
   (`raw/figures/<slug>-p<N>.md`) and **look at the PNG with the Read tool** before
   writing. Embed the ones that carry evidence on the source page as
   `![[raw/figures/<slug>-p<N>.png]]` next to the claim they support, with a sentence
   saying what the figure shows (axes, series, trend) taken from what you see, not from
   the machine description. A page render is a whole page: say which part matters.
   Quote numbers read off a chart as approximate and attribute them. If the PDF has
   figures but no `figures:`, tell the user `clip-pdf.mjs --figures-only` can add them.
   Never edit or add to `raw/figures/`.
3. Before creating a concept, search the proposed title, equivalent wording and
   nearby passages. Extend the canonical page, add a genuinely equivalent alias,
   or explain the new concept's distinct scope. Use `_templates/concept-note.md`;
   follow the directly linked efficacy reference for aliases and relationships.
   Create a stub (`status: stub`) only for an identified gap. Explain each useful
   connection under `## Relationships`; keep supporting citations in `sources:`
   and the relevant prose. Relatedness does not establish support. Update the
   task map the new knowledge helps answer. Preserve `reviewed` on pages that
   received only metadata/link edits; stamp it only after factual verification.
4. Regenerate the catalog: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/index-gen.mjs"`
   (never hand-edit index.md's generated fence). With another writer in the vault,
   add `--paths-file <ledger>` (the JSON array of pages this ingest wrote, from
   `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>`) so their
   uncommitted pages stay out of the catalog and their lines already in it stay in. Write the log entry by piping the
   narrative to `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/log-entry.mjs" --op ingest --title "<title>" --since <token>`
   (creates `log/<timestamp>-ingest-<slug>.md` in the resolved vault).
5. Never edit anything under `raw/`. Validate the derived pages' exact citation
   targets, source hashes, frontmatter and supported claims. Rerun
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs" --backlog` and compare the actual
   hash-join membership with the initial set. Eligible sources just summarized
   should leave that set; restricted captures do not become ingested by exclusion.
   Confirm already summarized sources and raw bodies remain unchanged.
6. **Close the operation:**
   Run `op-ledger.mjs show --since <saved-token> --out <ledger>` and read what it lists as
   unclaimed (another writer's pages, or one of yours you did not record), then
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op ingest --title "<what you ingested>" --since <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger>`
   Commits exactly the pages this ingest touched, as one revertable unit, and
   reports anything it deliberately left alone. Without `--paths-file` the close is refused while another operation is open. Then follow the shared completion contract to push your updates (`wiki-sync.mjs`, or `wiki-sync.mjs --op <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "<what you ingested>"` to close and push in one command) and verify remote publication. If the sync is refused because uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes (exit 3), read "Refused sync" in the [operations reference](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md): never reset, check out, stash or delete a file you did not write.
# Completion for vault mutations

Use this contract for every ordinary vault write, including standalone clipping,
authoring and applying triage decisions. Read-only search, query, health, freshness
and preview work do not open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes.

`index.md`'s generated catalog is derived: regenerate it with `index-gen.mjs`,
never hand-edit its fence or read-modify-write the file. Manual framing outside
the fence is preserved. A catalog already dirty from another writer remains
theirs: refresh safe project catalogs separately and report a deferred global
refresh rather than adopt foreign edits merely to close this operation.

**Own the update through verified publication.** An authorized wiki edit includes
validation, the scoped operation commit, and pushing to its configured upstream
with `wiki-sync.mjs`, followed by remote verification. Finish those steps without
asking a separate routine permission question. An explicit user instruction to
hold publication or keep the work local overrides this default. A local commit
or a closed token alone does not publish the update. If a remote is absent or sync
fails, report the work as unpublished with its exact next action. Never create a
remote or repository merely to satisfy this rule. A token is not resolved merely
because its file was deleted; account for the work and verify the outcome.

1. **Resolve scope and authorization.** Read the vault's instructions. Existing
   session authorization counts: a request to make a wiki update includes its
   normal commit-and-sync completion unless an explicit hold applies. A request to
   answer/search does not authorize filing a new page. Purge requires its specific
   reviewed plan and publication approval; do not replace those with this rule.
2. **Open before the first write.** Run `op-begin.mjs --op <op>` and save its token.
   On task resumption, reconcile a saved token before opening another one. Keep
   the operation type, title, owned-path ledger, log path and last completed phase
   with it so recovery can distinguish unfinished work from an already closed step.
   It snapshots already-dirty paths; `op-commit` excludes them. It does not isolate
   simultaneous edits to the same file. Coordinate overlapping targets; preserve
   pre-existing changes and report exclusions instead of sweeping them into a commit.
   With concurrent writers, maintain an explicit ledger of the exact vault-relative
   files this operation owns, including its log and generated catalogs when safe.
   Let the writers keep it: give `--since <token>` to every clipper, to `log-entry.mjs`,
   to `index-gen.mjs` and to `refresh-catalogs.mjs --apply`, each of which records the
   exact path it writes (unquoted UTF-8, so a name with an em dash survives), and record
   a page you wrote with your own file tools using `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token>

3	
4	# Capture named sources and research selections
5	
6	A named URL or file request starts here, without broad web discovery or perspective
7	fan-out. Capture-only work never creates derived source or concept pages. For a
8	format-specific source, read its route before capture: [PDF](clip-pdf.md),
9	[Word](clip-docx.md), [PowerPoint](clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheet](clip-xlsx.md),
10	[GitHub repository](clip-gh.md), or [Confluence](clip-confluence.md).
11	Only read the matching route, then use its actual result and the shared completion
12	contract. The HTML mechanics below apply to ordinary web pages and supplied pages.
13	
14	## Named sources
15	When the user names the pages to capture (URLs or saved files), there is nothing to
16	search for: skip broad research and discovery scoring. Dedup still applies to
17	the exact pages they named:
18	- Check them: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/known-urls.mjs" --check "<url>" "<url>"`
19	  (read-only; it needs no operation). The lines come back in the order given and carry no
20	  URL, so match them by position. `new`: clip it. `clipped raw/clippings/<name>.md`: it is
21	  already in the vault, so say so; if the user wants a second, dated copy of a page that has
22	  changed, clip it with `--recapture` (see the result table below).
23	  `declined: <reason>`: leave it, unless the user says the decline no longer holds; then
24	  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/decline.mjs" supersede "<url>" --reason "<why>"`, or
25	  `--supersede-decline="<why>"` on the clip.
26	- Clip the new ones using the capture procedure below, with `--topic="<topic>"` (the topic as the user gave it),
27	  `--quality=<tier>` and `--since <token>` on every clip.
28	- A page the user rejects is recorded, not forgotten:
29	  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --decline="<one-line reason>"`.
30	- Use the capture and completion contract below: open a discover operation
31	  before the first decline or clip, pass its token as `--since`, finish the capture
32	  with `op-ledger.mjs show` and `op-commit`. Ingest only when the exact source set
33	  is already authorized; a capture-only request ends after verified capture publication.
34	- A page the clipper cannot read (a login, a consent wall, an age check, a thin
35	  extraction) is saved by the user from a signed-in browser and supplied with
36	  `--from-file` (below).
37	
38	## Capture the selected sources
39	Use the operation opened before the first decline or clip. If none is open, run
40	`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op discover` before clipping
41	and retain its token; never overwrite a saved token. Do prerequisite and duplicate
42	checks first. When there is nothing to capture or decline, return without opening
43	an operation. Read-only named-URL dedup does not require broad coverage research.
44	
45	For each kept candidate:
46	`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>`
47	
48	**Pass `--topic` on every clip in the run, and use the same string for all of
49	them** — it is what lets maintainer triage group this run's leftovers together
50	later. Use the topic as the user gave it ($ARGUMENTS); do not re-word it per
51	source, or one run becomes several groups. The flag feeds both places a topic
52	can land: the clipping's frontmatter when the clip succeeds, and the triage log
53	when it fails, so you never have to know which happened.
54	
55	**"Every clip" includes the non-HTML ones.** A candidate that is a PDF, a Word
56	file or a spreadsheet does not go through `clip.mjs` — it goes through
57	`clip-pdf.mjs`, `clip-docx.mjs` or `clip-xlsx.mjs` (see [PDF capture](clip-pdf.md) and
58	[Word capture](clip-docx.md)), and **every one of those takes `--topic` too**:
59	
60	```bash
61	node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs"  "<file.pdf>"  --source="<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
62	node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-docx.mjs" "<file.docx>" --source="<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
63	node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-xlsx.mjs" "<file.xlsx>" --source="<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
64	# clip-pptx.mjs takes the same options; clip-pdf also records the figure files it renders (--figures)
65	```
66	
67	**A Confluence Cloud URL is HTML but also does not go through `clip.mjs`** — it
68	requires authentication `clip.mjs`'s anonymous fetch does not have, and reads
69	as thin content / gets auto-declined. Route it to [Confluence capture](clip-confluence.md) instead
70	(only applies if the `confluencer` plugin is installed — an optional runtime
71	dependency this one clipper alone takes on; see that reference for why):
72	
73	```bash
74	node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-confluence.mjs" "<confluence-url-or-page-id>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
75	```
76	
77	Binary capture routes need the same topic string as HTML routes. Topic is
78	recorded going forward only; missing attribution leaves the resulting rows under
79	Unattributed. For a one-off named source outside a research run, omit the topic
80	rather than inventing one.
81	
82	It blocks unreliable domains, skips dupes, extracts via Defuddle, and writes
83	`raw/clippings/<slug>.md` with `source`, `created`, `tags:[clippings]`, `quality`,
84	`topic`, `source-hash`. A `thin content` result means the page was a SPA/paywall — clip.mjs
85	records the decline automatically; report it for manual clipping (the user saves the page and you supply it with `--from-file <path>`, adding `--override-decline` because the decline was automatic), don't retry
86	blindly. A page that is a login form, a consent wall or an age check is not clipped even when it is long: its own vocabulary dominates the text and none of its title is in it (`lib/interstitial.mjs`). It is queued as `wrong-node` and is NOT declined, because a wall is not a verdict on the source; save it from a signed-in browser and supply it with `--from-file <path>`. A URL that looks like a text file (a checksum manifest, a pinned source file, anything on the raw GitHub host) is kept whole in a fence with `extraction: plaintext`, never judged thin; a binary or a file over 1 MiB served as text is refused and queued as `attention`. A `failed` result (403/transient) is NOT auto-declined — it may recover,
87	and a 180-day TTL would bury a source you still want.
88	
89	**What a clip result means.** `clip.mjs` prints one result per URL:
90	
91	| Result | Meaning | What you do |
92	|---|---|---|
93	| `clipped: raw/clippings/<name>.md` | written | cite that path |
94	| `duplicate (already clipped)` | this URL is already in the vault, also when another session wrote it first | nothing; do not clip it again. To keep a second, dated copy of a page that has changed, run the clip again with `--recapture` |
95	| `unchanged (same text as raw/clippings/<name>.md); nothing written` | `--recapture` found the page's text identical to a capture already held (exit 0) | nothing; the page has not changed |
96	| `recapture: not clipped yet, clipping it normally: <url>` | `--recapture` on a URL that was not in the vault; the line is followed by the ordinary result | read the result that follows |
97	| `clash: <url>: raw/clippings/<name>.md already exists ...` | the URL is new but every name it could have had was taken; **nothing was written** and one `attention` row is queued in triage | open the file named in the line and read its `source:` to see what holds the name, then re-run with `--slug=<name>`, or leave the row for maintainer triage |
98	| `declined`, `blocked`, `thin content`, `failed` | see below | see below |
99	
100	A taken file name is a `clash`, never a `duplicate`: a `duplicate` always means the same URL.
101	
102	**A second capture of a page already clipped.** `clip.mjs "<url>" --recapture --since <token>` fetches the page and runs the usual checks. If the text is new it writes a second clipping beside the first, named as the oldest capture's own name followed by ` (recaptured YYYY-MM-DD)`, with the same suffix on its `title`, `recapture-of` naming the newest existing capture, and `created` today; the older clipping is never edited. A second recapture on the same day with different text is a `clash`. `--slug=<name>` with `--recapture` is used exactly, with no suffix. Without the flag the same URL is a `duplicate`.
103	
104	**A page a person saved.** `clip.mjs "<url>" --from-file <path> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>` records a page saved from a signed-in browser, with its real URL as `source` and nothing fetched. The file is `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt` (the page text) or `.html` or `.htm` (read by the same extractor as a fetched page), at most 1 MiB. The clipping carries `extraction: manual` and `supplied-sha256`, the SHA-256 of the file's bytes; the file's name is not recorded. The thin, login-form and decline checks apply as to any clip: a page under 100 words is queued as `thin` and is never declined, and a login, consent or age-gate page is queued as `wrong-node` and not written. A missing file, a folder, an empty path or an extension that is not one of those exits 2; a binary file or one over 1 MiB is queued as `attention`. `--from-file` on a URL already clipped is a `duplicate`, and with `--recapture` it writes a dated recapture. The clipper's refusal lines for a thin, wrong-node or login, consent or age-gate page say to use this route. `apply-reclips` refuses a clipping with `extraction: manual` (listed as refused, not a failure); to refresh one, save the page again and run `--from-file <path> --recapture`. The login-form check compares the page's title with its text, and it cannot judge a title with no word of five letters or more, for example a URL that ends in a bare id; a gate page supplied at such a URL is not caught.
105	
106	**Names.** A page's title names its file. A document with no title and no heading is named from its URL path, nearest folder first, so `.../skills/one/SKILL.md` is `one-SKILL.md` and `.../skills/two/SKILL.md` is `two-SKILL.md`; the bare last segment is used only after the folders. The frontmatter `title:` stays exactly what the extractor returned, so `title: ""` on such a clipping is not a defect. A new clipping never ends `.md.md`; an older one may, and its name is still valid. A title another clipping already holds gets the distinguishing URL part added, for example `Smith v. Jones (93-1260.ZO)`. `--slug=<name>` chooses the file name without `.md`; a taken name is a clash and is never suffixed. `clip-pdf`, `clip-docx`, `clip-pptx` and `clip-xlsx` also take `--title="<text>"`, for a file whose name is not its title (`valve.pdf`), and `--slug=<name>`.
107	
108	An option a clipper does not know exits 2 with its usage and clips nothing; `--help` prints the usage and clips nothing.
109	
110	**Every unresolved link is queued for triage automatically.** `clip.mjs` records
111	`failed`, `thin`, and `wrong-node` outcomes to `.wiki-master/triage.jsonl`, so a
112	link that needs a human survives the terminal scrollback. Do not rely on your
113	completion report to carry them — point the user at [maintainer triage](../../wiki-maintainer/references/triage.md), where they can
114	disposition each one (retry, decline, clipped-by-hand). Queue anything else that
115	needs their judgement yourself with `recordIssue(vaultPath, { url, kind:
116	'attention', reason })`.
117	
118	## Finish capture and report
119	Show the ranked list (title, url, quality, why), which clips succeeded, and which
120	were skipped (blocked, duplicate, thin, failed). If issues were queued, mention
121	maintainer triage and report their counts.
122	
123	**Finish the capture operation before any decision pause.** The clipping set is what
124	the clippers recorded, not something to rebuild afterwards: run
125	`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" show --since <saved-token> --out <ledger>`
126	and read its `raw/clippings/...` entries, exactly as written (a name with an em dash
127	included). The number of `raw/clippings/` entries must equal the number of clippings the
128	`clipped:` results reported (one per URL or file; `clip-gh` reports a file count, and
129	`clip-pdf --figures` adds `raw/figures/` entries that are not clippings); if it does not,
130	stop and find the difference. Never rebuild the set from `git show`, whose default output
131	quotes and escapes a non-ASCII name. Write one discovery log entry naming the
132	clipped/declined/failed counts (`log-entry.mjs ... --since <saved-token>`), run `show`
133	again, and close with:
134	`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op discover --title "<topic> → N clipped" --since <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger>`.
135	The `<ledger>` file you wrote outlives the close, so the ingest that follows takes its
136	clipping set from it.
137	Without `--paths-file` the close is refused while another operation is open. Verify the commit and push and verify remote publication through the shared
138	contract (`wiki-sync.mjs --op <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "<topic>"` closes and pushes in one command). If no writes occurred, report that and do not manufacture a log/commit.
139	Clippings must not remain dirty while waiting for an ingestion decision.
140	
141	Then use the existing authorization for this exact source set:
142	- **Discover-and-ingest already authorized:** read [ingestion](ingest.md) and process the named
143	  successful clippings immediately. It owns a fresh operation and its own log.
144	  No second confirmation is needed.
145	- **Only discovery or capture authorized:** report the captured set and stop; do
146	  not create derived pages. If ingestion is subsequently requested, use the named
147	  set in a fresh operation.
148	- **Ingestion declined:** retain the committed clippings for manual review.
149	
150	## Guardrails
151	- The perspective passes never write the vault; the matching clipping helper is the sole writer to its raw artifacts.
152	- Never edit the **body** of anything under `raw/` — clipped content is immutable
153	  source-of-truth. Frontmatter is pipeline state and may be updated by wiki-master
154	  tooling only (never by hand, never the body).
155	- Prefer primary/authoritative sources over open-publishing platforms.
156	- Ingestion requires authorization for this scope; existing explicit authorization
157	  satisfies this ingestion boundary. Do not add another confirmation to an approved discover-and-ingest run.
158	# Ingest captured evidence
159	
160	Read [access and host commands](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md) before touching the vault. Also read for this operation: [evidence](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md).
161	Load the rest only when this run reaches it — [efficacy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md) before creating or merging a concept, alias or relationship; [maintenance](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md) when you compute the backlog with the content-hash join, or hit a structural repair.
162	Before the first authorized write, follow the shared operations completion contract; reuse existing session authorization.
163	
164	## Select eligible work before opening an operation
165	
166	For an explicit request to process new/un-ingested clippings without a filename,
167	run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs" --backlog`. The **not ingested
168	(no summary records their hash)** list is the starting set. This source-hash join,
169	including its documented legacy fallback, is authoritative for membership; do
170	not infer backlog from filenames, navigation citations or a successful exit.
171	An unspecified request to use the researcher role is not a request to ingest all.
172	
173	For named clippings, resolve and read those exact paths only. Check the same
174	hash-join report and the existing source summaries before doing work: if a source
175	page already records that clipping's `source-hash`, preserve it and report already
176	ingested. A rerun creates no duplicate summary or unearned second ingestion.
177	An explicit request to revise an existing summary can update that canonical page;
178	do not expand named ingestion to unrelated backlog or broad discovery.
179	
180	Inspect each selected clipping's metadata before treating it as support. Exclude
181	`citation-status: quarantined`, `restricted` or `retired` evidence, preserving its
182	raw bytes and restriction; report it separately rather than summarizing it as
183	accepted support. A missing source hash is a repair issue, not permission to
184	invent one. Binary originals and figure sidecars are not summary targets. The
185	helper's backlog can include restricted or defective captures, so its count is
186	not automatically the count of eligible work.
187	
188	If the backlog is zero, every named source is already summarized, or no eligible
189	source remains, stop and report the actual result and any exclusions. Do not
190	create pages, open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes. For work that
191	remains, retain the exact eligible set and initial hash-join membership. See
192	[backlog semantics](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md) for migration
193	and repair cases; structural repair still needs its own authorized scope.
194	
195	## Ingest and complete the selected set
196	
197	Read [operation completion](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md)
198	before the first authorized write.
199	
200	**Open the operation first:** `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op ingest`
201	This records what was already uncommitted, so the commit at the end contains your
202	work and not the user's in-progress writing. Close it in step 6.
203	
204	**Keep the ledger as you go.** Record each page you write (`wiki/sources/...`, a concept
205	or synthesis you create or change) with
206	`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" add --since <token> <path>...`, and give
207	`--since <token>` to `index-gen.mjs` and `log-entry.mjs`. When this ingest follows a discover
208	run, take the clipping set from that run's ledger file (its `raw/clippings/...` entries), not
209	from `git show`. Delegated writers get the parent token in their brief and run the same `add`
210	for the pages they write; they never close the operation (see the operations reference).
211	
212	Prefer a named clipping set; two concurrent ingests can overwrite shared concept
213	pages, so coordinate overlapping targets rather than processing the global backlog
214	in parallel. Update only pages substantively changed by the evidence.
215	
216	Apply the [Reddit and Medium evidence policy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md#reddit-and-medium)
217	to every page you write: Reddit-derived content belongs under
218	`## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` and Medium-derived content under
219	`## Medium articles`, including when updating a mixed-source page.
220	
221	For each eligible source, perform steps 1–3 and preserve raw body bytes. After
222	the selected batch, perform steps 4–6 once so the operation has one log and commit:
223	1. Read the exact clipping through the guarded CLI or filesystem. Write derived
224	   Markdown through exact-path filesystem edits, never a whole CLI `content=` payload. Discuss
225	   the key takeaways with the user.
226	2. Write/update `wiki/sources/<slug>.md`: a summary with `sources: ["[[<raw link>]]"]`,
227	   `type: source`, `ai-generated: true`, and typed `created`/`updated`/`reviewed`.
228	   **Always quote each wikilink inside the list — `sources: ["[[A]]", "[[B]]"]`,
229	   never a bare `sources: [[A]]` or an unquoted block list (`- [[A]]`).** Both
230	   unquoted shapes look correct and Obsidian still renders the links, but neither
231	   is valid YAML: `[[A]]` is flow-sequence syntax one level too many and silently
232	   parses into a nested list instead of a string, which is exactly the "type
233	   mismatch, expected list" defect `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-inline-sources.mjs"`
234	   exists to repair in bulk. Quoting is what makes it an unambiguous string.
235	   **Cite the clipping by its actual filesystem path — `sources: ["[[raw/clippings/<exact filename>.md]]"]` — copied from the path you just read, never retyped from
236	   the source's title.** The clipper slugifies a title into a filename (`/`, `:`,
237	   `#`, `*`, `?`, quotes and brackets all become `-`, then a 120-char cap), so any
238	   title carrying one of those characters or running long does NOT name its own
239	   file. Citing the remembered title produces a link to a file that does not exist:
240	   the page becomes a `provenanceGap` and its clipping reads as unparsed, even
241	   though the ingest itself was correct. List the resolved vault's exact `raw/clippings/` directory or reuse the path
242	   from step 1 rather than reconstructing it.
243	   Also record `source-hashes: [<sha256>, …]` — the `source-hash` frontmatter value
244	   of each clipping you summarized (read it from the clipping's frontmatter). This
245	   is the machine key the ingest-backlog metric joins on — immune to filename and
246	   citation drift; the `sources: ["[[…]]"]` wikilink stays for navigation.
247	   To repair vaults that already drifted this way:
248	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-provenance-links.mjs"` (dry run) then `--apply`.
249	   **Figures.** If the clipping's frontmatter lists `figures:`, open each sidecar
250	   (`raw/figures/<slug>-p<N>.md`) and **look at the PNG with the Read tool** before
251	   writing. Embed the ones that carry evidence on the source page as
252	   `![[raw/figures/<slug>-p<N>.png]]` next to the claim they support, with a sentence
253	   saying what the figure shows (axes, series, trend) taken from what you see, not from
254	   the machine description. A page render is a whole page: say which part matters.
255	   Quote numbers read off a chart as approximate and attribute them. If the PDF has
256	   figures but no `figures:`, tell the user `clip-pdf.mjs --figures-only` can add them.
257	   Never edit or add to `raw/figures/`.
258	3. Before creating a concept, search the proposed title, equivalent wording and
259	   nearby passages. Extend the canonical page, add a genuinely equivalent alias,
260	   or explain the new concept's distinct scope. Use `_templates/concept-note.md`;
261	   follow the directly linked efficacy reference for aliases and relationships.
262	   Create a stub (`status: stub`) only for an identified gap. Explain each useful
263	   connection under `## Relationships`; keep supporting citations in `sources:`
264	   and the relevant prose. Relatedness does not establish support. Update the
